newsitem.title: GREECE: DRACHMA BROADLY STABLE VS MAJOR EMS IN 97 - SOURCE.
newsitem.headline: DRACHMA BROADLY STABLE VS MAJOR EMS IN 97 - SOURCE.

text.p: The Bank of Greece will stick to its pre-announced anti-inflationary exchange rate policy by keeping the drachma broadly stable against major currencies making up the ecu, a high-level central bank official told Reuters.
"The exchange rate policy remains anti-inflationary and is consistent with the central bank's pre-announcouced monetary policy goals," the official said.
The central bank announced its 1997 monetary policy objectives in late January, making the stability of the drachma vis-a-vis the major currencies that make up the ecu its main intermediate target.
"The behaviour of the drachma against the major currencies that make up the ecu and the ecu itself is consistent with this goal," the official said.
The drachma was slightly down, 0.02 percent, against the mark and 0.38 percent up versus the French franc from December 31, 1996 to June 11.
It was also marginally higher versus the Italian lira, the Dutch guilder, the Spanish peseta and the Portuguese escudo.
The drachma fell 10.36 percent vis-a-vis the dollar and 15.50 percent against the yen over the same time span.
It retreated 0.81 percent against the ecu from end-1996 to June 11 but had dropped by more than 1.80 percent against the ecu in May before rebounding.
Ecu/drachma has been fluctuating in the 309.00-310.20 range in the last few days.
Asked whether the wider fluctuation of the drachma against the ecu this year signalled a policy shift in the highly visible ecu/drachma rate, the official said "this is not so."
"The drachma firmed more than 1.0 percent against the ecu during 1996 before settling 1.0 lower at end-1996, in line with the central bank's target," he said.
Bank of Greece had said it wanted the drachma to be broadly stable against the ecu in 1996 and delivered on it.

"The behaviour of ecu/drachma parity is consistent with the central bank's policy goal. The evolution of the ecu drachma exchange rate in recent weeks reflects primarily the strength of the pound sterling," the official added.
The drachma slid 6.40 percent against the pound from end-96 to June 11 based on fixing rates. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
